title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 — Section 146: Necessity for insurance
content: Section 146(1) states that a person must not use, or permit another person to use, a motor vehicle in a public place unless an insurance policy meeting the requirements of Chapter XI is in force for that use. This is the statutory third-party insurance requirement. It does not by itself establish that damage to the insured vehicle is covered; check the issued policy and its own-damage section.

title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 — Section 147: Requirements of policies
content: Section 147 describes the requirements for policies covering specified third-party liabilities, including death or bodily injury and damage to third-party property caused by or arising from use of a motor vehicle in a public place. The exact policy terms, insured persons, limits, and applicable law must be checked for a specific situation.

title: IRDAI Bima Bharosa — Policyholder grievance FAQs
publisher: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
content: IRDAI's Bima Bharosa FAQ says policyholders should first approach the insurer's Grievance Redressal Officer in writing, include supporting documents, and keep written acknowledgement. The FAQ currently says the insurer should resolve the complaint within 15 days. If the response is unsatisfactory or no resolution is provided within that timeline, the FAQ describes approaching IRDAI through its grievance cell or Bima Bharosa portal. Confirm the current process and contact details on the official portal before acting. The portal warns it does not ask complainants or policyholders for payments.
